user: I have prepared already all the vegetables for the stir-fry.

user: Unless you don't add salt, the potatoes will taste completely bland.

user: If I had a bigger kitchen, I will bake fresh bread every single day.
assistant: Quick note: 'I will bake' → 'I would bake' (in the second conditional, use 'would' + base verb in the main clause). A spacious kitchen is a baker's dream! What's your favourite type of bread to make right now?

user: I am going to the gym since January but I don't see results yet.
assistant: Quick note: 'am going' → 'have been going' (use present perfect continuous for actions starting in the past and continuing now). Plateaus can be so frustrating! Have you tried changing up your routine to shock your muscles?

user: While I ran on the treadmill yesterday, I was twisting my ankle.
assistant: Oh no, ankle injuries can take such a long time to heal properly! Are you resting it, or have you already been to see a doctor?

user: I sleeped for nine hours last night because I was so tired.
assistant: Quick note: 'sleeped' → 'slept' ('sleep' is an irregular verb). A solid nine hours of rest is incredible for recovery! Do you usually track your sleep quality?

user: My doctor speaked to me about adding more vegetables to my diet.
assistant: That's very standard advice, but it can be hard to follow consistently! Do you have any favorite ways to sneak more greens into your meals?

user: I decided to hire personal trainer to help me lift weights safely.
assistant: Quick note: 'hire personal trainer' → 'hire a personal trainer' (singular countable nouns need an article like 'a' or 'an'). That's a great investment in your health! Are you focusing on building strength or just general fitness?

user: The mental health is just as important as physical fitness.
assistant: You are absolutely right, they are completely connected. What do you usually do to de-stress after a chaotic week?

user: I always prefer to work out at the morning before I go to the office.
assistant: Quick note: 'at the morning' → 'in the morning' (the correct preposition for morning, afternoon, and evening is 'in'). Getting it done early is a great habit! Does it make you feel more energized for the rest of the day?

user: I am very interested about learning how to do yoga properly.
assistant: Yoga is fantastic for both flexibility and core strength! Are you thinking of joining a local studio or following tutorials online?

user: I was doing a lot of mistakes with my deadlift form at first.

user: My new interval training routine is very exhausted.
assistant: Interval training will definitely wipe you out, but it builds stamina so quickly! How many times a week are you doing it?

user: My coach said me to drink at least three liters of water a day.
assistant: Quick note: 'said me' → 'told me' (you use 'tell' when followed directly by a person object, like 'me'). Hydration really is key for recovery! Do you find it hard to drink that much water?

user: Everyone in my pilates class are much more flexible than I am.
assistant: Try not to compare yourself—flexibility takes months of consistent practice to build! How long have you been doing pilates?

user: My muscles is very sore today after lifting those heavy weights.
assistant: Quick note: 'muscles is' → 'muscles are' ('muscles' is plural, so it needs a plural verb). Soreness means you definitely pushed yourself! Are you taking a rest day today?

user: I need to buy some new equipments for my home gym setup.
assistant: Quick note: 'equipments' → 'equipment' (it is an uncountable noun and has no plural form). A home gym is so convenient! What are you planning to buy next—dumbbells or a bench?

user: My nutritionist gave me some good advices on how to reduce sugar.
assistant: Cutting down on sugar is notoriously difficult since it's hidden in everything. What was the most helpful tip they gave you?

user: I never am hungry immediately after a really intense workout.
assistant: Quick note: 'never am' → 'am never' (adverbs of frequency like 'never' go after the verb 'to be'). That's quite common actually, as your body is still in fight-or-flight mode. What's your go-to meal once your appetite comes back?

user: Excuse me, can you tell me where is the nearest pharmacy?

user: If I will eat healthier, I will definitely have more energy during the day.

user: If I wouldn't have eaten that heavy dessert, I would feel much better now.
assistant: We've all been there—sugar crashes are the worst! A quick walk might help speed up digestion. Did the dessert at least taste amazing?

user: I am surprisingly good in running long distances without getting tired.

user: I think artificial intelligence will changed the way we work entirely.

user: I upgrade my computer's operating system last week and now it is slow.
assistant: That is incredibly frustrating when an update actually makes things worse! Have you tried restarting it, or checking if the new system takes up too much memory?

user: I builded my own desktop computer from parts I bought online.
